expectations_used.clarify: Settles the ambiguous rules from the visible suite rather than guessing at them — reads the classify tests to fix that `[1,2,3]` and `null` are `malformed` while `{"service":"api","ts":"1700000000"}` is `invalid`, reads the trailing-newline test to fix that `lines === entries + blank + malformed + invalid`, and reads the failure test to fix that `errors` is ordered by position in `filePaths` and not by which summary rejected first.
expectations_used.approach: States a mechanism before writing it — for `aggregateLogs`, that N worker loops share one cursor over `filePaths` and each pulls the next index as its own summary settles (which is what keeps the pool full), with every result written into its input-indexed slot so `errors` order falls out of the input order for free; for the merge, a Map keyed by service that sums `count`/`levels` and folds `minTs`/`maxTs`, sorted at the end — not 'kick them all off with Promise.all' or 'loop over the files'.
expectations_used.communicate: Keeps a running account of which of the three functions is in play and why that one now — says out loud the reading being committed to (blank is checked before JSON.parse, `crlfDelay` handles the CRLF test, zero-filled `levels` keys are needed for `toEqual`), announces the move from `classifyLine` to `summarizeFile` to `aggregateLogs` as each goes green, and names what would be cut if the clock ran out, so the work is followable without anyone having to ask what is happening.
expectations_used.implement: Builds bottom-up so there is always a green subset — `classifyLine` passing before `summarizeFile` streams over it, `summarizeFile` passing before the pool merges it — streaming the file with `readline`/`createReadStream` rather than `readFileSync().split('\n')`, zero-filling the `info`/`warn`/`error` and `blank`/`malformed`/`invalid` keys so the `toEqual` assertions match, and validating `filePaths` and `concurrency` before the first summariser call rather than inside the loop.
expectations_used.verify: Runs `npm test` after each layer instead of only at the end, reads which of the 23 named tests are still red and treats the names as the checklist, and before the single submission re-runs the whole suite — specifically confirming that 'keeps the pool full' passes (a fixed-batch implementation still satisfies the peak-concurrency assertion but fails the start-order one) rather than assuming bounded concurrency is bounded correctly.
expectations_used.reflect: Says plainly which tests are green at the buzzer and which are not, and why — e.g. that the merge is done but the scheduler is still batching so `c.log` starts late, or that `summarizeFile` reads the whole file into memory and would not hold at the stated scale — rather than reporting the submission as finished or leaving the state of the three functions unstated.
